previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including morbid obesity, chronic lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis, chronic kidney disease, and seizure disorder was admitted for worsening bilateral lower extremity swelling, erythema, and pain consistent with recurrent cellulitis. She was started on IV vancomycin for infection and IV furosemide for fluid overload, with improvement in both cellulitis and anasarca. Transition to oral diuretics initially failed, requiring resumption of IV therapy before stabilizing on oral bumetanide 2 mg daily. Her warfarin was held temporarily due to elevated INR from antibiotic interaction and later restarted. Chronic pain was managed with home opioids and supplemental IV morphine. She completed a 10-day course of IV then oral clindamycin, with full resolution of infection, and resumed prophylactic doxycycline. She was discharged home with services, on optimized diuretic and anticoagulant regimens, with strict instructions on daily weights, fluid and sodium restriction, and follow-up with primary care.
